clue.text: Back in a moment

definitions.meaning: to back a proposal is to support it formally, as a seconder does
a very short instant of time, as in 'wait a tick'

explanation.definitionFit: Supporting a motion is seconding it, and a brief instant of time is also this sixtieth of a minute.

clue.text: Sort of net used by French watermen

definitions.meaning: a large fishing net hanging vertically, weighted at the bottom
the river flowing through Paris, used by French boatmen

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a vertical fishing net and the river that bargemen navigate through Paris.

clue.text: A clergyman, not a comedian

indicators.note: not a says the article is taken away from the word for the clergyman

parts.note: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution

explanation.surface: Someone insists he is a priest rather than a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' deletes an A from CHAPLAIN. The surface says the comedian is denied; in fact he is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie, the silent-film star of The Tramp, is the most famous screen clown of all.

clue.text: No good at all for use in a riot

indicators.note: letters running riot are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something is useless even as a weapon in a street disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or criminal, so thoroughly bad in character.

clue.text: Large revolver protects the entertainers

parts.note: a spinning top is a toy that revolves

explanation.surface: A big gun keeps the performers safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a pistol, but here it is a toy that spins. The definition is descriptive: a circus tent shelters the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circus tent is the canvas shelter under which clowns and acrobats perform.

clue.text: Badly riled, but he does nothing

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very annoyed, yet just sits around.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is a loafer.

clue.text: Modify a painting technique

parts.note: to temper something is to moderate or modify it

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to change their method.
explanation.definitionFit: This method binds pigment with egg yolk, used for medieval panel paintings.

clue.text: Charge sheet?

parts.note: a charge sheet is a police record of accusations, but here a charge is a cost and the sheet lists them

explanation.definitionFit: A document setting out what goods cost is a list of charges.

clue.text: Animal with a head for heights

definitions.text: Animal with a head for heights

parts.words: Animal with a head for heights
parts.note: a head for heights usually means not fearing them, but here it is a creature whose head is literally held very high on a long neck

explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked African grazer carries its head higher than any other land creature.

clue.text: Imply small company is involved in game, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters become involved, tangled together into a fresh order

parts.note: CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a small firm is mixed up in some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved' signals the anagram of IMPLY with CO; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The four-yearly international sporting festival gives its name to such a contest, so a game is an example of it.

clue.text: A watch and a clock that can't be relied on?

definitions.text: A watch and a clock that can't be relied on?

parts.words: A watch and a clock that can't be relied on?
parts.note: a watch and a clock make two timepieces, and two unfaithful lovers are also described by this term

explanation.definitionFit: People who cheat on partners are unfaithful, and two timekeeping devices are literally a pair of timers.

clue.text: Open hostility

parts.note: reads as overt enmity, but 'open' is a verb: to begin hostilities formally

explanation.definitionFit: A nation formally announcing armed conflict is the act that starts fighting officially.

clue.text: Calm, yet still quits

definitions.meaning: calm and level, as an unruffled temper
used for emphasis, as in 'better still' or 'more so'
being quits means owing each other nothing

explanation.definitionFit: A level temper is placid, the word intensifies a comparison, and when debts are settled neither side owes anything.

clue.text: Wild dog in Australia

parts.note: a straightforward description of the native feral canine of the Australian outback

explanation.definitionFit: This tawny feral canine is native to the Australian bush.

clue.text: Relaxing one's guard is risky

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters, letting them fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters ONES, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Letting your defences down is hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relaxing' rearranges ONES and GUARD; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous carries a likelihood of harm.

clue.text: It's a man found shipwrecked on a Pacific isle

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up, so these letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A castaway washes up on an island in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipwrecked' signals the anagram of ITSAMAN plus the second A; 'found' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island state south of mainland Australia lies where the Pacific meets the Southern Ocean.

clue.text: Army signalling?

parts.note: the question mark hints at signalling by arms, waving flags held at different angles

explanation.definitionFit: This flag system sends letters by the positions of the signaller's arms.

clue.text: US representative ambiguously masculine? I quit!

indicators.note: something ambiguous can be read in more than one way, so these letters are rearranged
the speaker saying 'I quit' means the letter I leaves the word

explanation.surface: Someone says a figure representing America is vaguely manly, and resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I quit' removes I from MASCULINE, leaving MASCULNE; 'ambiguously' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded top-hatted figure is the traditional personification of the United States government.

clue.text: Taking offence

parts.note: taking offence normally means feeling insulted, but here it is the crime of taking property

explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the criminal offence of taking another person's goods.

clue.text: Climb Everest, say

definitions.meaning: to climb is to go up, ascend
Everest is an example of a mountain, for which this is an old word

explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is the verb, and as a noun the word is a poetic term for a peak such as the Himalayan giant.

clue.text: Move up into a form that's per feet

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters into a new arrangement, a form

explanation.surface: An instruction to go up to a higher class at school that is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges UPINTOA; 'form' (a school class) completes the surface. 'per feet' is a scanning error for 'perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal society imagined as flawless is called after Thomas More's imaginary island.

clue.text: It's not cheap, love

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means costly and is also an affectionate way of addressing someone.

clue.text: Game to get down to bare essentials

definitions.text: Game to get down to bare essentials

parts.words: Game to get down to bare essentials
parts.note: 'get down to bare essentials' sounds like cutting to the point, but here it means players literally undressing as they lose

explanation.definitionFit: In this card game losers shed clothing, eventually reducing themselves to almost nothing.

clue.text: Fish in shallow water

definitions.meaning: a large group of fish swimming together
a sandbank or shallow place in the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a school of fish and a sandbar where water is not deep.

clue.text: Source of inspiration from sister at Oxford

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sibling studying at the university inspires someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'sistER AT Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Muse of love poetry, and Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspired artists.

clue.text: Bedroom layout reveals lack of attention

indicators.note: a new layout of the letters, as a room's contents might be laid out afresh

explanation.surface: The arrangement of a bedroom shows that nobody was concentrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layout' signals rearranging BEDROOM; 'reveals' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Weariness from lack of interest means the mind wanders and attention lapses.

clue.text: Soldier seen in pub? It makes sense

indicators.note: the soldier is seen inside the pub, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a local is a person's regular pub

explanation.surface: An American serviceman spotted at the bar seems perfectly reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is the British name for the nearby pub you usually drink in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rational and coherent is reasoned soundly, so it adds up.

clue.text: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors

definitions.text: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors

parts.words: A dangerous choice for mythological sailors
parts.note: refers to Odysseus having to steer between a six-headed monster and a whirlpool, both perilous options

explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the many-headed sea monster opposite Charybdis gave sailors one of two deadly options in the strait.

clue.text: Penthouse let on a new arrangement

indicators.note: these words are given a new arrangement, an order different from the one printed

explanation.surface: A luxury top-floor flat is rented out under fresh terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penthouse' suggests a luxury flat, but its older sense is a sloping shed built against a wall; 'on' as well as 'a' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of penthouse is a sloping-roofed shed attached to the side of a building.
